items.title: A bound on the degrees of the elliptic decomposition of a function with N poles
items.author: Thomas Dreyfus; Julien Roques
items.work: Galois Groups of Difference Equations of Order Two on Elliptic Curves
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma bounds the degrees of a decomposition f = A(weierstrass_k) + weierstrass_k' B(weierstrass_k) for a function f in M_{k Lambda} with at most N poles counted with multiplicity: the numerator and denominator of A have degree at most 2N, those of B at most 2N+3 (statement lines 614-624). The proof reduces to the Lambda-periodic case by scaling, writes f through its even and odd parts, and reads the bounds off two pole counts: the even part has at most 2N poles and its reduced denominator contributes as many poles through the zeroes of Q(weierstrass), while the numerator is bounded by applying the same argument to the reciprocal and using that elliptic functions have equally many zeroes and poles; the odd part is handled the same way with the factor weierstrass' (proof lines 626-647). The step that carries the content is the passage from pole counts to degree bounds, which is the classical zero-pole bookkeeping for elliptic functions; the reduction and the odd part are then the same computation. H2.
